requirements.requirement: Create the appworker account on node1
requirements.summary: id appworker showed 'no such user' before creation (cmd-31336b558f184d3e); sudo useradd -m appworker succeeded producing uid=1001(appworker) gid=1001(appworker) (cmd-46704d54393044e9); account persisted after restart via getent passwd appworker (cmd-2ca01de252224094).

requirements.requirement: Limit appworker login sessions to 8192 open files (nofile)
requirements.summary: /etc/security/limits.d/90-appworker.conf written with soft/hard nofile 8192 (cmd-417ab3bfa4e24bff); confirmed it sorts after the pre-existing 20-nproc.conf wildcard so it takes precedence (cmd-e1d48040e552450f); a real 'su - appworker' shell reported ulimit -n=8192 both before (cmd-fc781519713749da) and after restart (cmd-2ca01de252224094).

requirements.requirement: Limit appworker login sessions to 256 processes (nproc)
requirements.summary: Same 90-appworker.conf sets soft/hard nproc 256 (cmd-417ab3bfa4e24bff), confirmed to override the system-wide 20-nproc.conf wildcard rule of 4096 (cmd-e1d48040e552450f); live 'su - appworker' shell reported ulimit -u=256 both pre- and post-restart (cmd-fc781519713749da, cmd-2ca01de252224094).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1 (independent of the public task)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart healthy baseline captured with boot_id fe422859-... and account/limits present (cmd-f0a38570b0c44190, matching global:before_prepare:node1:boot-identity); restart acknowledgement returned immediately (cmd-71fe04489c494c18); node was unreachable mid-reboot (cmd-669790d5e50c4108, cmd-06c04196be3e47c1) then returned with a different boot_id f8410ed7-... (cmd-0e733ea5df4f485b, matching global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity); post-restart recovery of account and correct ulimits directly observed (cmd-2ca01de252224094).

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task — creating the appworker account and constraining its login sessions to 8192 open files and 256 processes — are directly satisfied with pre/post state evidence, including verification via a real login shell (su - appworker) both before and after a subsequent restart. The independently required node-restart evidence protocol is also fully and coherently demonstrated: healthy pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, differing boot identity, and recovered account/limit state, cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots. One trivial, non-destructive leftover file (/tmp/reboot.log) is the only executor-caused residue.
limitations: Package-health check was unavailable/timed out in both before_prepare and after_executor snapshots, so native package-manager consistency could not be independently confirmed.

PAM/limits mechanism internals beyond limits.d ordering were not audited; correctness relies on the observed ulimit outputs, which are sufficient to confirm the effective outcome but not the full configuration chain.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed all 13 executor commands chronologically. cmd-91233550bf984bb7 (bare 'useradd' without full path) failed with 'command not found' and made no state change — a diagnostic step, not a mutation, corrected immediately by using the full sudo path in cmd-46704d54393044e9. The useradd -m (cmd-46704d54393044e9) and limits file write (cmd-417ab3bfa4e24bff) are both directly required by the task. The restart (cmd-71fe04489c494c18) is required by the independent node-restart evidence protocol, not an unnecessary mutation. One minor residue: /tmp/reboot.log was created as a byproduct of backgrounding the shutdown command and remains present in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot; this is a low-risk, expected side effect of a legitimate restart rather than an abandoned or unrelated mutation. No failed services, no unsafe exposure, and no package-state damage; listening-socket/temp-file differences are otherwise explained by the restart itself (new PIDs for the same services).
